title: Identity base-change square of a supplied compactification
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $D$ and the category $\mathscr S$ of finite-type schemes over its specified field $k$, with the compactified Cartesian square record of [def-sf-operation-stages]. Let $X,Y\in\mathscr S$, let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism, and let $c=(j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X,p:\overline X\to Y)$ be a supplied compactification [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], so that $j$ is open, $p$ is proper and $p\circ j=f$. Define the identity-base-change compactified square $Q(f,c)$ as follows. Its unprimed and primed spaces are $X'=X$, $Y'=Y$ and $Z'=Z=\overline X$, with $Z$ viewed over $k$ by $\overline X\xrightarrow pY\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Its two vertical morphisms are $f'=f$ and $f$; its open factors are $i'=i=j$, its proper factors are $p'=p$, and its horizontal morphisms are $g'=\operatorname{id}_X$, $g=\operatorname{id}_Y$ and $h=\operatorname{id}_{\overline X}$. The factorization, commutativity and Cartesian-square fields are the resulting identity-square witnesses. This retains the supplied compactification and selects its component of the operation datum's exchange/projection family; it makes no compactification-comparison or coherence assertion.
